# Establishment log — popol-vuh-014 (image 0045 from line 9, 0046, and 0047 to line 42)

Read 2026-11-26 from source/pages/i0045 (from l.9, after `… xuꜭhax cut capoh.`), all of i0046, and i0047 lines
1–42, in strips of about five lines at 0.8–1.1×, with 1.6–3.5× crops of every doubtful word, checked word by word
against Brasseur 1861 (OCR lines 23455–23500, 23560–23600, 23660–23700, 23730–23790).
Start: `Are chic xchi ca ꜩihoh calaxic Hunahpu, Xbalanque.` (0045 l.9–10, Ximénez's indented heading). End:
`… Hunahpu Coy xqui zuah.` (0047 l.41–42). **The part ends at Ximénez's own paragraph break**: 0047 l.43 is an
indented paragraph, `Catepuch xebixanic, xezuanic, xecohomanic …` (the grandmother's four trials), where
popol-vuh-015 should begin. Image 0048 was not needed.

parts.json: popol-vuh-015 images set to 0047–0050 (first_image 47, last_image 50, cite `LoC images 0047–0050`), as
011's–013's runs did for the next part; 016 is untouched (its run, or 015's, adjusts it).

Content: the heading (now the birth of Hunahpu and Xbalanque); Xquic gives birth on the mountain without the old
woman; the babies cry and are put on an anthill, then on thorns, where Hunbaꜩ and Hunchouen want them dead out of
envy; they are not let into the house and grow up on the mountain; Hunbaꜩ and Hunchouen are great flautists,
singers, painters and carvers, who know their younger brothers' nature but are blinded by envy; the twins only
hunt with the blowgun, are not loved and are fed last, take no offence; their birds are eaten by the elder
brothers; one day they come without birds: "they are caught in the tree, let our elder brothers climb for them";
the twins plan to change their elders' being; at the tree Cante the elders climb, the tree grows, they cannot
come down; told to loosen their loincloths and tie them behind, the cloths become tails and they become monkeys
and go off into the forest; the twins come home and tell the grandmother; she grieves; they say she will see
their faces again, it is a test, she must not laugh; they begin to play the tune Hunahpu Coy.

## Folios
Counting as 004–013 did (0045 = 18r): 0046 = 18v, 0047 = 19r → `fols. 18r–19r`. The crop of 0046 carries `18` at the
top left (the folio doubt in QUESTIONS.md, 2026-11-24, again); the earlier count is kept.

## Paragraphs
Ximénez indents only the heading (0045 l.9) and `Arecut calaxic vae` (0045 l.11) in this stretch; the further
paragraphs are cut at speech turns and episode joints, as 011–013 did.

## Letter rule used (002–013's rules, unchanged)
- g-shaped → ꜭ: `qui ꜭoheic` ×2 (0046 l.8, l.31; B. qoheic), `que be ta cuꜭ` (MS `cug`), `ruꜭ catit, ruꜭ pu qui
  chuch` (MS `rug`), `iuvꜭ` (see below); gh → ꜭh: `xꜭha`, `xeꜭha` (all but `xecha` ×2, below), `xe vꜭhax` ×2
  (MS `xevghax`).
- q-shaped `qux` → `ꜭux` (009's rule): `chi qui ꜭux` ×2 (0045 l.41, 0046 l.36), `vyoc qui ꜭux`.
- q-shaped + u where Brasseur has g → ꜫ, u dropped: `vꜫih calaxic` (0045 l.12, MS `vquih`), `hutaꜫih` ×2 (MS
  `hutaquih`, as 007), `qui ꜫih` (0047 l.40, MS `quiquih`), `vꜫexel` (0045 l.38, MS `vquexel`; house vꜫexel).
- tresillo → ꜫ: **`qui ꜫaꜫvachibal`** ×2 (0045 l.25–26, l.44; B. cakvachibal 'envy'): both letters clear 3-shapes
  at 2.2×, as 012's `ꜫaꜫ` where Brasseur also has cak; `que loꜫoxic` (0046 l.2, MS 3-shaped; B. logoxic).
- tz ligature (with its ascender) → ꜩ: `xchi ca ꜩihoh`, `He a ꜩaca vloc` (2.2× crop, ascender clear), `quiꜩih`,
  `Hunbaꜩ` throughout, `chuꜩin`, `Xa ca ꜩolcomih`, `ca ꜩih ta`, `Vꜩ bala` ×2, `vꜩ chic`, `vꜩam` ×2, `vꜩ i binic`,
  `ivaꜩ` ×2, `xꜩeenic`, and `caꜩ` 'elder brothers' throughout (B. c'atz).
- tz' (ligature with the comma) → ꜯ: `ꜯiquin` throughout, the house word (B. tziquin).
- plain z (ʒ, no ascender) kept as z: `zanic` ×2 (B. zanic), `zac`, `zu` ×2, `ahzu` ×2, **`ahzibab`** (0045 l.35;
  B. ahtzibab; the stroke above is the h's ascender; as 012's `vzibel`, 013's `xa zibanic`), `zaquiric`, `zach`,
  `xzipoh` (0047 l.2, at the line end), `qui zilah`, `huzu`, `zuanic`, `xqui zuah`, `xbizonic` (B. bizonic).
- q-shaped + u kept as written where Brasseur has g: `quz cu qui varam` (0045 l.20; B. guz), as 012's `quz`.
- plain c kept where Brasseur has g, q or k: `capoh`, `qui chac` throughout (B. chag), `ri caꜩ`, `catit`/`ratit`
  (B. k'atit), `cazah` ×2 (B. kazah), `cah` 'come down' (B. kah), `chacan` (B. ch'akan), `chu cab tac che` (B. gab;
  as 012), `vyoc` (B. yog), `icalaba` (B. galaba; as 013's `xe a calaba`), `ahcot` (B. ahqot), `cucaam`, `iucaam`,
  **`xa coy`** (0047 l.17, B. qoy) and `Hunahpu Coy` (see below), `Catecut`/`Catepuch` (B. Qate…).

## Names and spellings
- `Hunahpu, Xbalanque` throughout; `Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen` throughout (the MS has `hunchoven` at 0045 l.23 and 0046
  l.3, 5, 11; printed `Hunchouen` as 009–013); `Xquic`; `Xibalba`.
- **`Cante`** (0046 l.39, the tree): capitalised as a name (B. Cante; his note: 'yellow wood', not a K'iche' word).
- **`Hunahpu Coy`** (0047 l.41, the tune): MS `hunahpu` + a struck letter (a crossed z/4-like stroke) + `coy`. The
  struck letter is not printed, as 013's struck letter at 0044 l.38; `coy` with plain c, as `xa coy` at 0047 l.17
  (house ꜭoy 'monkey'; B. Hunahpu-Qoy). The struck letter may be a cuatrillo that Ximénez himself replaced, or
  the cuatrillo itself written as a 4 beside c; doubtful. Capitalised as the name of the tune.
- `huiub` ×2 (0045 l.17, l.29; MS `huiub`) beside `huyub` ×2 (0047 l.18–19): both as written.

## Doubtful readings and decisions against Brasseur
- 0045 l.11 `xchi ca biyh` (MS `xchicabyh`, a mark over the y): printed `biyh` as 008–013.
- 0045 l.12 `Ta xuric` (MS `taxuric`; B. `ta x-u riq`): one word.
- 0045 l.19 `qui chi` (MS `quichi` with a raised t-like mark over `chi`, taken as Ximénez's heavy accent, as 013's
  `huvi`).
- 0045 l.20 `Catecut ta xe ya pa zanic` (MS `pazanic`; B. `pu zanic`): MS a.
- 0045 l.21 `Xe el chicu chiri` (MS `chicu`; B. `chi cu`).
- 0045 l.29 **`xe quiy vi`** (MS `xequiy vi`, y with a descender and two dots, at 2.2×; B. `x-e quim vi`). Printed as
  written; presumably ꜭiy 'grow' (the drafter decides). Doubtful.
- 0045 l.30 `E cu nimac ahzu` (MS a heavy blot over one letter before `ahzu`): the blotted letter is not printed.
- 0045 l.31 `Xe nimaquir` (MS `xenimaquir`, the r small and raised).
- 0045 l.32 `rail` (MS `raíl`, an accent on the i; B. rail).
- 0045 l.35 `ahcot` (MS `ah cot`, a space; agent nouns joined, as `ahzu`, `ahbix`, `ahzibab`).
- 0045 l.45 **`xcah vi vyoc`** (MS `xcahvi` with the raised accent over `vi`, then `v yoc`; B. `x-kah vi u yog`):
  at 3.5× the `vi` is clear; `vyoc` joined as `vbi`.
- 0046 l.1 `Xa cu vvbanic` (0045 l.47 `xacu-` + 0046 l.1 `vvbanic`; B. `u ubanic`); `vvbanic` again at 0046 l.41.
- 0046 l.2 **`rumal ri ratit`** (MS `ri ıatit`: the first letter of the word is an i-like stroke with a hook, taken
  as Ximénez's r, with B. `r'atit`). Doubtful (it may be `ri atit` with a stray stroke).
- 0046 l.4 **`xhaninac vaim`** (the first letter after x has a closed loop like b; B. `x-haninak`): read h with
  Brasseur. Doubtful.
- 0046 l.6–7 `oiouaric` (MS `oio-|uaric`; B. oyovaric).
- 0046 l.18 `xcacar curi atit` (MS `xcacarcuri atit`; `curi` as 013).
- 0046 l.19 **`iucaam`** (MS `iucaam`, u not v; B. `yv caam`): the 2nd-plural i- joined, as 004's `ivumal`, with
  the letter as written (as 004's `iuecha`).
- 0046 l.22–23 `xꜭha cut` (singular, MS `xgha`) for the twins' first speech; `xeꜭha cut` after the second.
- 0046 l.23 `Macu habi` (MS `macu habi`; B. `ma-cu-habi`).
- 0046 l.27 **`coh be iuvꜭ`** (MS `iuvg`, four letters at 2×; B. `yvuq`): printed as written. Doubtful.
- 0046 l.32 **`qui ꜭoheic, eu pam`** (MS `eupam` at 2×; B. `eu pam`, his French 'et (la forme de) leur ventre'):
  `eu` left undivided. Doubtful (it may be `e u pam`).
- 0046 l.33 `mi xqui ban` (a blot after `xqui`, not a letter).
- 0046 l.42 **`que chitihc`** (MS `chitihc` at 2×, no vowel between h and c; B. `chititic`): printed as written.
  Doubtful; perhaps a slip for `chitihic`.
- 0046 l.45–46 `ri ca ꜯiquin e maui` (MS `rica ꜩi-|quine maui`; B. `ri ka tziquin e mavi`).
- 0046 l.46 **`xa hix cazah vloc`** (MS `xahix`; B. `xa h'yx`): `hix` as written (`hix` occurs once in an earlier part).
- 0047 l.1 `xe acanic` (MS `xeaca-|nic`; B. `x-e akanic`).
- 0047 l.2 `xzipoh vpam` (MS `xʒi-|poh vpam`, the z at the line edge without an ascender; B. `x-zipoh`).
- 0047 l.7 `ix ca chac` (MS `ixcachac`); `Tocob ca vach` (MS `tocob cavach`; B. `togob ka vach`): plain c.
- 0047 l.9 `xecha vloc` and l.14 `xecha cut`: plain ch in the speech tag, as written (013's `xcha cut`).
- 0047 l.11–12 `chi xima xe i pam; nahlic vꜩam` (MS `xeipam na-|hlic vꜩam`; B. `xe y pam nahlic u tzam`).
- 0047 l.12 **`chi hure he chivih`** (MS `chihurehe chivih`; B. `ch'y hure he ch'yvih`): divided with Brasseur, `he`
  'tail' as `qui he` at l.16.
- 0047 l.13 `catecut vꜩ i binic` (MS `vꜩibinic`; B. `utz y binic`).
- 0047 l.15 `xqui huruba` (MS `xquihuruba`; B. `x-qui hurüba`).
- 0047 l.18 **`xebe chuvi tac che`**: MS `chui` with a raised t-like mark over the i (as 0045 l.19), the v not
  written; printed `chuvi` with Brasseur and the five other `chuvi` of this part. A dropped letter (README 5b);
  the drafter's note gives the MS form.
- 0047 l.18 **`chuti huyub`** (MS `chu` + a tall looped letter with an accent + `huyub`; B. `chuti huyub`): read t
  with Brasseur. Doubtful.
- 0047 l.20 `que vohon chic` (a blot after `chic`, not a letter); `qui zilah` plain z.
- 0047 l.31–32 `mi xin icalaba, mi pu xin ichiquiba` (MS `mixinicalaba`, `xinichiquiba`; B. `mi-x-in y galaba`):
  the 2nd-plural i- joined (004's rule); `mi xiban` ×2 likewise.
- 0047 l.36 `Mi xbizonic, ix catit; xchivil chic` (MS `mixbizonic ixca`^k`tit xchivil`; a small raised k over
  `catit`, not printed; B. `M'yx bizonic, yx Katit; x-ch'yvil`).
- 0047 l.37 `xque vlic` (MS `xquevlic`; B. `x-que ulic`).
- 0047 l.39 **`Cahhana qui ꜫih`** (MS `cahhana` at 2×, two h; B. `C'a na qui gih`): printed as written, undivided.
  Doubtful.

## Abbreviations
None expanded (the `chui` at 0047 l.18 is printed `chuvi`, above).

Nothing set aside; no gap.
